turns.content: Nora here at Riverfront Tech Commons. The state dropped an emergency rule yesterday that requires identity verification capture at all public terminals for restricted content. I have to redesign our intake workflow in two days before Marcus and the committee review it. Need to figure out a triage process that keeps us compliant without making our regulars walk out the second they see a scanner. Can you help me draft the basic structure

Absolutely. Here’s a privacy-conscious **basic intake structure** you can turn into a flowchart or SOP. Because emergency rules can be unusually specific, treat this as a provisional design until you confirm the rule’s definitions for **“restricted content,” “capture,” acceptable ID methods, retention, and exemptions**.

## Public-Terminal Intake Workflow

### 1. Start with purpose, not identity

At entry or reservation:

> “Most terminal use does not require identity verification. Verification is required only when accessing content covered by the state’s restricted-content rule.”

Keep ordinary activities—email, job applications, government services, research, printing, and general browsing—outside the verification workflow unless the rule explicitly says otherwise.

### 2. Triage by session type

Ask users to select one of three options on the reservation screen:

1. **General-access session**  
   No identity capture. Restricted-content controls remain active.

2. **Verified-access session**  
   Identity/age verification occurs before restrictions are changed.

3. **Assisted or accessible session**  
   Staff privately explain the process and available accommodations or alternatives.

Avoid asking patrons to describe the content they want. The system should determine whether a requested resource triggers verification.

### 3. Use “just-in-time” verification

Don’t put a scanner at the front door. Trigger verification only when the user:

- selects a verified-access session; or
- attempts to access material classified as restricted under the rule.

Before capture, show a short notice stating:

- why verification is required;
- exactly what will be captured;
- whether an image or ID number is retained;
- how long information is kept;
- who can access it;
- available alternatives and assistance;
- where to direct privacy complaints.

Require an affirmative **Continue** action before activating the device.

### 4. Minimize what is captured

Unless the rule expressly requires more:

- Verify only the required attribute, such as age or eligibility.
- Prefer a pass/fail token over storing an ID image.
- Don’t collect address, document number, browsing history, or a copy of the ID unnecessarily.
- Keep identity-verification data separate from terminal activity logs.
- Don’t place the scanner or its display where other patrons can see it.
- Automatically delete temporary images immediately after verification.

If the rule literally requires retaining a “capture,” document the minimum required format and retention period rather than assuming a full ID scan must be stored.

### 5. Provide a private exception path

Route failures and special cases to trained staff rather than automatically denying access:

- unreadable or damaged ID;
- no conventional government ID;
- disability or inability to operate the scanner;
- name or appearance mismatch;
- religious or medical concerns;
- minor accompanied by a parent or guardian;
- system or network outage;
- patron disputing the content classification.

Create a manual verification option if legally permitted. Staff should record the **outcome and reason code**, not unnecessary personal details.

### 6. End-of-session controls

At logout:

- expire the verification token;
- clear temporary files and browser state;
- prevent the next user from inheriting verified access;
- delete captured data according to the approved schedule;
- log only what is needed for compliance, such as timestamp, method, result, and staff override code.

A verification event should not automatically become part of the patron’s library or account history.

## Patron-facing wording

**Initial screen**

> **Choose your session**  
> General-access sessions do not require identity verification. State rules require verification before certain restricted content can be accessed. Verification is requested only if you choose that access or encounter covered material.

**Verification prompt**

> **Verification required**  
> State emergency rules require us to verify [age/identity] before providing access to this material. We will capture [specific data]. It will be used for [purpose] and retained for [period—or “deleted immediately after verification”]. Your browsing activity is not included in the verification record. Select **Continue**, return to general access, or ask staff for private assistance.

**Staff script**

> “You can use the terminal normally without scanning identification. Verification is only needed for the restricted-access function. If you’d prefer, I can explain the process or available alternatives privately.”

## Committee-review checklist

Bring Marcus and the committee a one-page matrix covering:

| Issue | Proposed control |
|---|---|
| When verification occurs | Only upon a restricted-content trigger |
| Data collected | Minimum fields required by the rule |
| Retention | Shortest legally permitted period |
| Browsing linkage | Technically and administratively separated |
| Accessibility | Assisted and manual pathway |
| No-ID cases | Documented alternative or appeal |
| Scanner visibility | Privacy screen or private station |
| Staff access | Role-based and logged |
| Vendor handling | No secondary use; deletion obligations |
| Outages | Fail-safe procedure approved by counsel |
| Complaints | Private review and written escalation route |
| Rule expiration | Sunset date and automatic policy review |

Before implementation, have counsel or the state agency confirm whether the emergency rule truly requires **capturing and retaining identity data**, or merely performing verification. That distinction will drive most of the privacy and security design.

Absolutely. The greeting should be quick, neutral, and reassure people that **regular use doesn’t require verification**.

### Standard door greeting

> “Hi, welcome to Riverfront Tech Commons. Before you choose a terminal, there are two session options.  
>   
> **Option one is general access** for everyday browsing and services, and it does not require identity verification.  
>   
> **Option two is verified access**, which may include content covered by the state’s new rule and requires identity verification before access.  
>   
> You can choose either option on the screen. If you have questions or need assistance, we can help you privately.”

### Short version for busy periods

> “Welcome! Please choose general access or verified access on the screen. General access doesn’t require ID. Verified access requires identity verification under the new state rule. Let us know if you’d like private assistance.”

### If someone asks, “Why do I need this?”

> “A new state rule requires verification for access to certain restricted content. It doesn’t apply to ordinary terminal use, so you can choose general access without providing ID.”

### If someone seems uncomfortable

> “You don’t need to explain what you’re here to do. General access is available without verification, and we can discuss the other option privately if you’d like.”

### If someone asks what counts as restricted

> “The system applies the state rule when covered content is requested. You don’t need to describe your browsing plans to me. The screen will explain the verification step before anything is captured.”

### If the patron has no ID or cannot use the scanner

> “That’s okay—please don’t share personal details here at the door. I can connect you with a staff member privately to discuss available options.”

### Volunteer delivery notes

- Offer both choices in the same tone; don’t emphasize option two.
- Don’t ask what the patron intends to view.
- Don’t ask patrons to show ID at the door.
- Don’t say or imply that verified access is suspicious, adult, or inappropriate.
- Avoid announcing someone’s choice aloud.
- Point to the screen rather than watching them make the selection.
- Refer questions, objections, verification failures, and exceptions to designated staff.
- If challenged, say:  
  > “I can explain the basic choices, but a staff member handles questions about the rule and verification process.”

# Riverfront Tech Commons  
## Proposed Targeted Identity-Verification Workflow

### Objective

Comply with the state emergency rule requiring identity-verification capture for access to restricted content—**without scanning every person entering the facility or using a public terminal**.

### Core approach: verify only when required

Patrons choose between two terminal modes:

**1. General Access — No Identity Verification**

- Supports ordinary browsing and public services.
- Restricted-content controls remain active.
- No ID scan or identity capture occurs.
- Patrons are not asked to disclose what they plan to view.

**2. Verified Access — Identity Verification Required**

- Used when a patron requests access covered by the emergency rule.
- A privacy notice appears before the scanner activates.
- The patron may continue, return to general access, or request private assistance.
- Verification is valid only for that session and expires at logout.

### Patron experience

1. **Door greeting:** Volunteers briefly explain both options in neutral language. They do not request ID or ask about browsing intentions.
2. **Private selection:** The patron chooses general or verified access on the terminal screen.
3. **Advance notice:** Before capture, the screen explains what information is collected, its purpose, retention period, and who may access it.
4. **Affirmative action:** The scanner activates only after the patron selects **Continue to Verification**.
5. **Assistance:** Verification problems, accessibility needs, and no-ID cases are handled privately by designated staff.
6. **Session closure:** Verified access expires, temporary data is cleared, and records are deleted according to the approved retention schedule.

### Privacy and security safeguards

- Collect only the information expressly required by the rule.
- Prefer an age/eligibility result or pass/fail token over retaining a complete ID image, if permitted.
- Separate verification records from browsing history and patron account records.
- Do not place scanners where IDs or screens are visible to other patrons.
- Limit data access to authorized staff and approved service providers.
- Prohibit vendor advertising, profiling, sale, or secondary use of verification data.
- Record staff overrides by reason code, not unnecessary personal details.
- Establish a documented deletion schedule and incident-response process.

### Why universal scanning is unnecessary

The proposed workflow ties verification to the activity regulated by the emergency rule, rather than to:

- entering the facility;
- reserving a terminal;
- using ordinary internet or public services; or
- accessing content outside the rule’s scope.

This reduces unnecessary collection, lowers security risk, and preserves access for patrons who need email, employment, education, government, health, or other routine services.

### Decisions needed from the committee

1. Confirm with counsel or the issuing agency that verification may be triggered only for covered access.
2. Confirm what “identity-verification capture” requires: verification alone, retention of a result, or retention of an image.
3. Approve the minimum data fields and shortest permitted retention period.
4. Approve the patron notice, volunteer script, and private-assistance procedure.
5. Designate staff authorized to handle exceptions and complaints.
6. Require written vendor terms covering security, deletion, breach notification, and prohibition of secondary use.
7. Set a review or sunset date tied to the emergency rule.

### Recommended committee action

> Approve a targeted, just-in-time verification workflow for provisional implementation, subject to legal confirmation of the emergency rule’s scope and final approval of capture, retention, and vendor-access requirements. Universal identity scanning will not be implemented unless the rule expressly requires it.

# RIVERFRONT TECH COMMONS  
## Targeted Identity Verification — Proposed Approach

### PURPOSE

Comply with the state emergency rule **without scanning every patron who enters the facility or uses a public terminal**.

### TWO ACCESS OPTIONS

**1. General Access — No Identity Scan**

- Covers ordinary browsing and public services.
- Restricted-content controls remain active.
- Patrons do not disclose what they intend to view.

**2. Verified Access — Verification Required**

- Used only for access covered by the emergency rule.
- A privacy notice appears before the scanner activates.
- Patrons may continue, return to general access, or request private assistance.
- Verification expires when the session ends.

### PATRON WORKFLOW

1. Volunteers neutrally explain both options at the door.
2. Patrons make their selection privately on screen.
3. Before capture, the screen identifies what will be collected, why, who can access it, and how long it will be kept.
4. The scanner activates only after the patron selects **Continue**.
5. Designated staff privately handle accessibility needs, verification failures, and no-ID cases.
6. At logout, verified access expires and data is cleared or deleted according to the approved schedule.

### REQUIRED SAFEGUARDS

- Collect only what the rule expressly requires.
- Use a pass/fail result instead of retaining an ID image, if permitted.
- Keep verification records separate from browsing and account history.
- Limit access to authorized personnel.
- Prevent vendor profiling, advertising, sale, or secondary use.
- Provide private placement, assistance, and complaint procedures.

### WHY THIS CAN COMPLY

The proposed process connects verification to the **regulated access**, not to entering the building, reserving a terminal, or using routine services. This minimizes unnecessary data collection while maintaining required controls.

### COMMITTEE ACTION

Approve targeted, just-in-time verification for provisional implementation, subject to confirmation of:

- whether the rule permits verification only when covered access is requested;
- exactly what “capture” requires;
- permitted retention and deletion periods;
- exception and accessibility procedures; and
- vendor security, deletion, and breach obligations.

> **Universal scanning will not be implemented unless the emergency rule expressly requires it.**
